enforcing_note: Enforcing since 2026-09-30: every counted unit is above the floor, so a unit below it, a total below it or a first-party file no test loads fails coverage_floor (full tier) and scripts/coverage.sh. Units are derived from the path (an engine crate, a plugin directory, a module), so a new crate or plugin is judged from its first file; the C and C++ of every plugin and the native kit count, JUCE and the other submodules do not. An exemption is for what cannot be instrumented at all, never for what is merely untested -- exempt for a unit, exempt_files for one file inside a counted unit -- and each is audited for a reason and a file that still exists.

exempt.modules/trance-gate: ui_chain.js, 1315 lines that run on the Move inside Schwung's shadow UI: it imports Schwung's own page controller, input filter and screen reader by their absolute paths on the device (/data/UserData/schwung/shared/...), which this repository does not carry, so nothing here can load it. engines/trance-gate/tests/smoke_ui.mjs runs every entry point against those shared sources (ctest tg_move_ui, engines/trance-gate/tests/ui.sh), outside this report. The module's DSP is tg-core and its C shell is tg-move, both counted. A real gap, stated rather than hidden.

exempt_files.plugins/_shared/ui/src/ReducedMotion.cpp: The system's reduced-motion setting where it is not Cocoa's: every line is inside #if ! JUCE_MAC, so a macOS build -- the one coverage runs on -- compiles it to nothing and no tracefile can name it. macOS's setting is ReducedMotion.mm, which is counted.
exempt_files.plugins/_shared/ui/gallery/Main.cpp: The gallery application's entry point: a JUCEApplication that opens a desktop window and runs the event loop until a person closes it, so no test binary links it (tests/ui links the gallery's pages, not the app). Everything it shows is counted: every page, through the kit's tests and their snapshots (tests/ui), and the frame and registry in Gallery.cpp (tests/ui/gallery.cpp). The --shots mode it adds writes pictures for a person to look at, which the snapshot tests already hold.
